title: CommandEnvelope
description: A request to change authoritative state. Every externally initiated mutating command requires an idempotency key scoped to actor, endpoint, and environment (docs/03). Replays return the original command result.

command_id.description: Unique identity of this command. Prefix cmd_.

command_type.description: Dotted command name, e.g. order.place or risk.halt.closed.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the payload contract. Consumers must tolerate additive fields; a breaking change requires a new major version plus dual-read/dual-write migration (docs/03).

correlation_id.description: Groups every command and event belonging to one logical workflow, across languages and processes.

causation_id.description: Identity of the command or event that directly caused this one. Null only for an externally initiated root command.

actor_id.description: Authenticated subject or workload identity. Authorization is always evaluated server-side; the UI, Telegram, and any agent are untrusted callers (docs/02, docs/25 §3.6).

environment.description: Target environment. Commands are namespace-isolated: dev, test, staging, paper, shadow, live. Live credentials are never available to lower environments (docs/01 §4, ADR-012).

idempotency_key.description: Required for every externally initiated mutating command. Scoped to actor, endpoint, and environment. Enforced by a database uniqueness constraint, never by application memory (docs/03, WI-123). Replays return the original result.

trace_context.description: W3C trace propagation fields. Propagated across every language boundary (docs/02).

payload.description: Command body. Validated against the contract named by command_type and schema_version.

x-invariants: A command is a request, never a state assertion. The server decides the resulting state.
actor_id and actor_type are supplied by the trusted edge, not by the caller. A caller-supplied actor is rejected, not sanitized.
No command may bypass the Risk Engine for a risk-increasing transition (docs/25 §3.1).
No command may clear a halt. Halt is monotonic (docs/25 §3.9).
